The brief suggested std.mem.copyForwards as the fix; the @memcpy was deleted instead (the copy was a no-op — bufPrint's bytes are already in place). Same outcome, fewer instructions, and the dead padding branch alongside it is removed too.

zig_formatting_discovery.finding: Zig 0.16 std.fmt {d} prints the sign for SIGNED integer types (i8/i16/i32): 12 → '+12', 0 → ' +0', -8 → ' -8'. Unsigned (u8) and comptime_int literals get no '+'. This is why the i8 legal_fixed cells render with explicit signs.
zig_formatting_discovery.consequence: the T327 golden (+12 / +0 forms) was correct and is unchanged; only its mechanism comment was wrong and is corrected. The T374 golden uses the same sign-always forms.
zig_formatting_discovery.consequence_2: values |v| >= 100 (e.g. i8 127 → '+127', 4 bytes) fail the 3-byte bufPrint and render '???' — pre-existing behavior, unchanged by this fix, unreachable at 4x4 (scores in [-16, 16]).

dead_branch_verdict.why: {d:>3} on success returns exactly 3 bytes (probe: every in-range i8 value → len 3); out-of-range values fail bufPrint → the catch branch runs. No success path has s1.len < 3.
